Husband gets stridhan criminal case quashed five years after divorce, Himachal Pradesh High Court

The Himachal Pradesh High Court has quashed criminal proceedings against a former husband accused of retaining his ex-wife's stridhan, holding that the alleged offence could not be treated as continuing indefinitely after the dissolution of their marriage.

The couple married in 2007 and began living separately around 2008. The wife alleged that her husband had retained her stridhan despite repeated demands since 2011. Their marriage was dissolved through an ex parte divorce decree in October 2012, but she filed a criminal complaint under Sections 406 and 506 IPC only in July 2017.

The High Court examined the limitation provisions under Section 468 CrPC and distinguished between judicial separation, where the marital relationship legally continues, and divorce, which formally dissolves the marriage.

The Court held that although retention of stridhan may constitute a continuing offence while the matrimonial relationship subsists, the same reasoning could not be extended indefinitely after divorce. Since the complaint was filed nearly five years after the divorce decree, it was held to be barred by the applicable three-year limitation period.

Accordingly, the High Court quashed the summoning order, notice of accusation and consequential criminal proceedings against the former husband. The decision concerned the limitation applicable to the criminal complaint and did not extinguish the wife's ownership rights over her stridhan or determine any separate civil remedy for its recovery.
